pr_title: Add new price sensors with API token access to pvpc hourly pricing
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

**3 New sensors added**, (they appear if the optional API Token for private access is enabled)
- **Injection price**: price of excess energy from self-consumption
- OMIE price: electricity price in the 'open' market
- MAG price: Temporal tax cost for gas compensation in Spain

this is a direct follow up of #85767 (containing the new optional API Token), enabled with the dependency bump done in #85612

closes #84071

#### Some details

* New sensors have the same attributes than the old PVPC sensor, except for some non-applicable tariff-related attribs, all handled in the external library
* New attributes 'data_id' and 'data_name' for all sensors to identify the data-source for each one
* Unique_id for old PVPC sensor is preserved (no breaking changes), and new ones have new ids
* When disabling/enabling sensors, `coordinator.api.update_active_sensors` sets the download handler to make only the necessary API calls

### The problem

Sorry is must not open here this is an "issue" before it happens

This affects this integration: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/pvpc_hourly_pricing/

I've received an email from esios about api.esios.ree.es telling that actually the access token is sent in this header:

    Authorization: Token token=xxxxxxxxx"

And now this header must be used:

    x-api-key: xxxxxxxxxx

There is a test endpoint to make testing: https://apip.esios.ree.es](https://apip.esios.ree.es

Below is the email received (in spanish).

Best


Received email:
```
Estimad@ minombre :-).

Como usuario/a del API público de esios api.esios.ree.es, le informamos que se va proceder a la migracion de dicho API a una nueva infraestructura.

El interfaz de todas las operaciones del api se mantendrá sin modificaciones, únicamente se produce un cambio en la cabecera donde se indica el token de acceso a la hora de realizar las llamadas al API.

Actualmente el token de acceso al API se incluye en la siguiente cabecera:

    Authorization: Token token=xxxxxxxxx"


La nueva cabecera a utilizar es la siguiente:

    x-api-key: xxxxxxxxxx


Hemos habilitado el siguiente endpoint de test para que pueda realizar las pruebas necesarias una vez adapte sus llamadas: [https://apip.esios.ree.es](https://apip.esios.ree.es")

Las dos cabeceras son compatibles tanto en el sistema actual como en el nuevo, por lo que ya puede dejar preparados desarrollos con ambas cabeceras si lo desea, y tenerlos actualizados para cuando se despliegue en producción el nuevo sistema.

Se comunicará más adelante la fecha de puesta en producción a través de la web [https://www.esios.ree.es](https://www.esios.ree.es") y por correo electrónico. Si ha adaptado sus llamadas con la nueva cabecera, el cambio debe ser transparente ya que se mantendrá el endpoint https://api.esios.ree.es.

Ante cualquier consulta, por favor pónganse en contacto por correo electrónico con [consultasios@ree.es](mailto:consultasios@ree.es")

Un cordial saludo,

Consultas SIOS.
```

review_comments: Why is `config_entry_id` optional when we make this assertion?
This should not be in an external API

Hi @emontnemery, I see. The logic in the external lib is this: 
(there are 2 methods to convert between sensor key and HA unique-ids)

```python
_ha_uniqueid_to_sensor_key = {
    TARIFFS[0]: KEY_PVPC,
    TARIFFS[1]: KEY_PVPC,
    f"{TARIFFS[0]}_{KEY_INJECTION}": KEY_INJECTION,
    f"{TARIFFS[1]}_{KEY_INJECTION}": KEY_INJECTION,
    f"{TARIFFS[0]}_{KEY_MAG}": KEY_MAG,
    f"{TARIFFS[1]}_{KEY_MAG}": KEY_MAG,
    f"{TARIFFS[0]}_{KEY_OMIE}": KEY_OMIE,
    f"{TARIFFS[1]}_{KEY_OMIE}": KEY_OMIE,
}


def get_enabled_sensor_keys(
    using_private_api: bool, disabled_sensor_ids: list[str]
) -> set[str]:
    """(HA) Get enabled API indicators."""
    sensor_keys = set(ALL_SENSORS) if using_private_api else {KEY_PVPC}
    for unique_id in disabled_sensor_ids:
        disabled_ind = _ha_uniqueid_to_sensor_key[unique_id]
        if disabled_ind in sensor_keys:
            sensor_keys.remove(disabled_ind)

    return sensor_keys


def make_sensor_unique_id(config_entry_id: str, sensor_key: str) -> str:
    """(HA) Generate unique_id for each sensor kind and config entry."""
    assert sensor_key in ALL_SENSORS
    if sensor_key == KEY_PVPC:
        # for old compatibility
        return config_entry_id
    return f"{config_entry_id}_{sensor_key}"
```

As you can see, the old `unique_id` was just the selected tariff, just to be able to configure an entry for each tariff. To handle the addition of new sensors I'm just composing tariff + sensor-key, but leaving the old one as it was, for backward compatibility. 

Should I resolve this logic in other way? Or it's ok if I just move those methods to the integration?
Move this logic to the integration please 👍
